mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-01.stem: Transistors are used to amplify small signals and control current switching on and off.
reasons: True. A transistor is used to amplify small signals or control current on and off. Do not treat it simply as another part that only passes current one way. Match the circuit role, specified component and terminal identification.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A transistor is used to amplify small signals or control current on and off. Do not treat it simply as another part that only passes current one way. Match the circuit role, specified component and terminal identification.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-02.stem: The 4Ms provide perspectives for investigating changes in manufacturing conditions; the classification does not establish that a newly assigned operator is the cause solely because personnel changed.
reasons: True. The manufacturing 4M are people, machines/equipment, materials/parts, and methods. Checking changes in conditions from these four perspectives helps reduce omissions when quality changes. This is not a classification for assuming that a new operator must be the cause. Check whether a tool change or material-lot change occurred at the same time.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The manufacturing 4M are people, machines/equipment, materials/parts, and methods. Checking changes in conditions from these four perspectives helps reduce omissions when quality changes. This is not a classification for assuming that a new operator must be the cause. Check whether a tool change or material-lot change occurred at the same time.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-03.stem: The fact that one of the 4Ms changed alone proves that change caused the problem.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A change occurring near a defect in time does not prove causation. Investigate other 4M changes and separate facts from hypotheses.
False. A change occurring near a defect in time does not prove causation. Investigate other 4M changes and separate facts from hypotheses.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-04.stem: When learning new work, understand not only the procedure sequence but also why that sequence is used.
reasons:
True. When learning new work, understand why the steps follow that order rather than only memorizing the sequence. Before practice, confirm the pre-work inspection, prohibited actions, and response to abnormalities.
In OJT, the instructor explains and demonstrates, the learner practices within the specified scope, and the instructor checks the result. Having seen a task is not the same as being able to perform it safely alone. If an operation is unclear, stop and ask before attempting it.
After listening, explaining the procedure back in your own words helps reveal misunderstandings. In particular, do not rely on a vague acknowledgment when confirming values, units, part orientation, and stopping conditions.
Reading this material does not replace the training or qualifications required at the workplace. Confirm the work you may perform and the required training with the responsible person according to the equipment and working conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When learning new work, understand why the steps follow that order rather than only memorizing the sequence. Before practice, confirm the pre-work inspection, prohibited actions, and response to abnormalities.
In OJT, the instructor explains and demonstrates, the learner practices within the specified scope, and the instructor checks the result. Having seen a task is not the same as being able to perform it safely alone. If an operation is unclear, stop and ask before attempting it.
After listening, explaining the procedure back in your own words helps reveal misunderstandings. In particular, do not rely on a vague acknowledgment when confirming values, units, part orientation, and stopping conditions.
Reading this material does not replace the training or qualifications required at the workplace. Confirm the work you may perform and the required training with the responsible person according to the equipment and working conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-05.stem: In the basic third-angle projection layout, the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. In basic third-angle projection, the view from the right is placed to the right of the front view, not the left.
False. In basic third-angle projection, the view from the right is placed to the right of the front view, not the left.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-06.stem: Even when smoke obscures the escape route, always continue firefighting if an extinguisher is available.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Initial firefighting requires a safe escape route. If that route is being lost, evacuate and report rather than persist with extinguishing.
False. Initial firefighting requires a safe escape route. If that route is being lost, evacuate and report rather than persist with extinguishing.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-07.stem: Protective glasses shield eyes from flying objects, but work requiring light protection, such as gas cutting, requires checking the specified shading performance.
reasons: True. Protective glasses guard the eyes against flying material and similar hazards. Tasks such as gas cutting also require the specified protection against harmful light. Match sleeves and gloves to the process, observing prohibitions such as no gloves at a rotating drill press. Do not apply one example outfit to every task.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Protective glasses guard the eyes against flying material and similar hazards. Tasks such as gas cutting also require the specified protection against harmful light. Match sleeves and gloves to the process, observing prohibitions such as no gloves at a rotating drill press. Do not apply one example outfit to every task.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-08.stem: Cost reduction permits unauthorized changes to specified materials.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even cost reduction must preserve required quality and safety; obtain prescribed approval for material changes.
False. Even cost reduction must preserve required quality and safety; obtain prescribed approval for material changes.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-09.stem: A milling machine rotates the tool and uses relative tool/workpiece movement to machine flats and grooves.
reasons: True. Cutting removes material with a tool to form the required shape. A lathe mainly rotates the workpiece against a tool to machine features such as outside diameters. A milling machine rotates the tool and uses relative movement between tool and workpiece to produce flats and grooves. A drill press rotates a drill to make holes. Distinguishing what rotates helps explain machine roles and danger areas.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Cutting removes material with a tool to form the required shape. A lathe mainly rotates the workpiece against a tool to machine features such as outside diameters. A milling machine rotates the tool and uses relative movement between tool and workpiece to produce flats and grooves. A drill press rotates a drill to make holes. Distinguishing what rotates helps explain machine roles and danger areas.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-10.stem: Actually reproducing a hazard and making contact with it is mandatory KYT practice.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. KYT teaches hazard prediction and action targets. Use safe materials rather than reproducing actual hazards or contacting them.
False. KYT teaches hazard prediction and action targets. Use safe materials rather than reproducing actual hazards or contacting them.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-11.stem: Understanding a machining center’s automatic tool-changing function does not automatically grant training or authorization for actual tool changes or operation.
reasons: True. Knowledge of machine construction and the scope of actual work permitted are separate; check training and procedures appropriate to equipment conditions.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Knowing a function’s name alone does not meet operating qualifications or work authorization, so the statement is not false.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-12.stem: Both the company and workers have occupational safety and health roles; appointing a safety representative alone does not eliminate hazards.
reasons: True. The source describes three aspects of occupational safety and health: standards for preventing harm, a system of responsibilities, and voluntary activities. Both the company and workers have roles. Naming a responsible person alone does not remove a hazard. Check whom you should consult and the emergency communication route.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source describes three aspects of occupational safety and health: standards for preventing harm, a system of responsibilities, and voluntary activities. Both the company and workers have roles. Naming a responsible person alone does not remove a hazard. Check whom you should consult and the emergency communication route.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-13.stem: Having the names of an occupational physician or safety representative makes worker reports unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even with specialist staff, workers’ observations need sharing. A representative’s name alone does not communicate an abnormality.
False. Even with specialist staff, workers’ observations need sharing. A representative’s name alone does not communicate an abnormality.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-14.stem: Quenching and annealing are the same treatment with different names.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Quenching aims at hardening, while annealing aims at softening, structure adjustment and related purposes. Distinguish objectives and heating/cooling conditions.
False. Quenching aims at hardening, while annealing aims at softening, structure adjustment and related purposes. Distinguish objectives and heating/cooling conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-15.stem: A sectional view can make internal holes and steps easier to understand than a view relying heavily on hidden lines.
reasons: True. A sectional view represents the inside of an object by imagining a cut and removing the portion in front. It can make internal holes and steps easier to understand than using many hidden lines. It is a way of communicating shape, not a machining instruction to cut the actual product.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A sectional view represents the inside of an object by imagining a cut and removing the portion in front. It can make internal holes and steps easier to understand than using many hidden lines. It is a way of communicating shape, not a machining instruction to cut the actual product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-16.stem: Do not merely memorize safety-sign shapes; also check the actions required at that location together with equipment procedures.
reasons:
True. Safety signs include those that prohibit actions, warn of a hazard, and indicate locations or equipment needed in an emergency. Do not only memorize the picture; consider what action is required at that location.
“No entry” does not mean you may enter if you are careful. An electric-shock warning indicates the presence of an electrical hazard. Follow the sign and confirm the equipment procedure and your authorization to enter the area.
For chemicals, check the container label and safety data sheet. Hazards such as ignition, corrosion, and health effects differ by substance. Do not identify contents solely by color or smell, or use liquid from an unlabeled container.
Check the locations and routes to fire extinguishers, AEDs, and evacuation areas during normal conditions instead of starting to search in an emergency. If an escape route is obstructed, request improvement according to workplace rules.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Safety signs include those that prohibit actions, warn of a hazard, and indicate locations or equipment needed in an emergency. Do not only memorize the picture; consider what action is required at that location.
“No entry” does not mean you may enter if you are careful. An electric-shock warning indicates the presence of an electrical hazard. Follow the sign and confirm the equipment procedure and your authorization to enter the area.
For chemicals, check the container label and safety data sheet. Hazards such as ignition, corrosion, and health effects differ by substance. Do not identify contents solely by color or smell, or use liquid from an unlabeled container.
Check the locations and routes to fire extinguishers, AEDs, and evacuation areas during normal conditions instead of starting to search in an emergency. If an escape route is obstructed, request improvement according to workplace rules.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-17.stem: Hollow plastic products are invariably manufactured by blow molding.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even among hollow products, a long tube of constant cross section can be a candidate for extrusion. Check geometry, material, quantity and approved process together.
False. Even among hollow products, a long tube of constant cross section can be a candidate for extrusion. Check geometry, material, quantity and approved process together.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-18.stem: Polishing addresses appearance, roughness, friction and other purposes, but stronger gloss is not necessarily better for every application.
reasons: True. Grinding removes small amounts of material using abrasive grains in a wheel and is used for hard materials or surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy. Polishing conditions a surface with abrasives and similar media. Its purposes include appearance, roughness, and friction, but a shinier surface is not necessarily better for every application. Check drawing requirements for size and surface condition separately.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Grinding removes small amounts of material using abrasive grains in a wheel and is used for hard materials or surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy. Polishing conditions a surface with abrasives and similar media. Its purposes include appearance, roughness, and friction, but a shinier surface is not necessarily better for every application. Check drawing requirements for size and surface condition separately.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-19.stem: If a diameter is within tolerance, parallelism may also be regarded as measured.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Diameter tolerance and parallelism are separate requirements. Verify geometrical tolerances using the relevant target and datum.
False. Diameter tolerance and parallelism are separate requirements. Verify geometrical tolerances using the relevant target and datum.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-20.stem: On a lathe, distinguish the chuck’s workpiece-holding role from the tool post’s cutting-tool-holding role.
reasons: True. The chuck grips the rotating workpiece while the tool post holds the cutting tool; their holding targets differ.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Treating workpiece-side and tool-side holders as the same can confuse reported locations or mounting targets, so the distinction is correct.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-21.stem: Protective equipment safe for one task is invariably safe for every other task.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Match protective equipment to each task’s hazards. For example, do not keep sheet-handling gloves on when operating a running drill press.
False. Match protective equipment to each task’s hazards. For example, do not keep sheet-handling gloves on when operating a running drill press.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-22.stem: Energy stored in a capacitor invariably becomes zero when the power display goes dark.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Energy may remain in a capacitor after power is stopped. Do not judge by the stopped-power display; obtain the prescribed checks.
False. Energy may remain in a capacitor after power is stopped. Do not judge by the stopped-power display; obtain the prescribed checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-23.stem: Read measuring-instrument graduations from directly in front because angled viewing can change readings through parallax.
reasons: True. Measurements are affected by the instrument, operator, temperature, setup, and other factors. Read the scale straight on because an oblique view creates parallax. Check calibration relating the indication to a reference, daily inspection records, and validity; a correct zero alone does not guarantee correctness across the full range.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Measurements are affected by the instrument, operator, temperature, setup, and other factors. Read the scale straight on because an oblique view creates parallax. Check calibration relating the indication to a reference, daily inspection records, and validity; a correct zero alone does not guarantee correctness across the full range.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-24.stem: If dimensions for the same location conflict, the operator may machine to their average.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. An average is not a formal requirement. Identify the conflicting location and ask the responsible person which dimension applies.
False. An average is not a formal requirement. Identify the conflicting location and ask the responsible person which dimension applies.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-25.stem: An observation of low pH does not mean the same thing as explaining that a substance lost electrons.
reasons: True. Oxidation and reduction can also be explained through electron transfer: losing electrons is oxidation; gaining them is reduction. Rusting iron and combustion illustrate oxidation, but some reactions have no visible change. A low pH observation does not mean the same thing as a statement that a substance lost electrons.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Oxidation and reduction can also be explained through electron transfer: losing electrons is oxidation; gaining them is reduction. Rusting iron and combustion illustrate oxidation, but some reactions have no visible change. A low pH observation does not mean the same thing as a statement that a substance lost electrons.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-26.stem: Ra and Rz can be compared directly by number if their units match.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even with identical units, Ra and Rz have different definitions. Compare using the same specified parameter and conditions.
False. Even with identical units, Ra and Rz have different definitions. Compare using the same specified parameter and conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-27.stem: If a 2:1 drawing labels a dimension 12, the actual size is 24 mm.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Written dimensions indicate actual size regardless of scale. A dimension of 12 specifies 12 mm; drawing at twice size does not make it 24 mm.
False. Written dimensions indicate actual size regardless of scale. A dimension of 12 specifies 12 mm; drawing at twice size does not make it 24 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-28.stem: Grounding forms part of equipment protection and relates to current paths during abnormalities such as leakage.
reasons: True. Grounding is part of an equipment protection system and affects current paths during faults such as leakage. Where a grounding conductor is specified, check its connection and report defects. Do not describe grounding as preventing leakage itself or removing every electric-shock hazard.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Grounding is part of an equipment protection system and affects current paths during faults such as leakage. Where a grounding conductor is specified, check its connection and report defects. Do not describe grounding as preventing leakage itself or removing every electric-shock hazard.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-29.stem: When replacing a resistor, do not decide a smaller component is suitable from resistance alone; also check specified ratings and operating conditions.
reasons: True. Identical resistance values can have different ratings or operating conditions. Smaller external size alone does not guarantee interchangeability with the specified part.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Identical resistance values can have different ratings or operating conditions. Smaller external size alone does not guarantee interchangeability with the specified part.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-30.stem: The operator may relax inspection criteria to maintain a target acceptance rate.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. An acceptance-rate target does not justify relaxing inspection requirements. Inspect to approved criteria and report uncertainties.
False. An acceptance-rate target does not justify relaxing inspection requirements. Inspect to approved criteria and report uncertainties.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-01.stem: Part of a cleaning-agent label is unreadable; a similarly shaped container is nearby. What should you do before use?
options: Assume the contents match the similar container.
Smell a small amount to investigate.
Mix it into another container before checking.
Withhold use and check identity, the SDS and instructions.
reasons: Identical container shapes do not necessarily mean identical contents.
Smelling an unknown substance can expose you to it.
Mixing unknown liquids can cause dangerous reactions or loss of identification information.
Withhold use and verify contents and handling using original identification, the SDS and approved instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-02.stem: A caliper reads in 0.05 mm increments; the main scale is 16 mm and the sixth vernier line aligns. What is the value?
reasons: This treats the sixth line as 0.06 mm without using the minimum reading of 0.05 mm.
This misreads the sixth line as 0.60 mm; 0.05 × 6 = 0.30 mm.
Main scale 16 + vernier 6 × 0.05 = 16.30 mm.
This adds line number 6 directly to main-scale value 16, ignoring the graduation quantity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-03.stem: The requirement is Ra 0.6 μm, but the only result given is Rz 2.4 μm. What should be done before judgment?
options: Obtain results for the specified Ra and conditions.
If dimensions conform, pass roughness too.
reasons: Ra and Rz are different parameters; obtain a result for the specified Ra and measurement conditions.
0.6 and 2.4 are values for different parameters and cannot be compared directly as numbers alone.
Rewriting measured Rz as Ra creates a record differing from the actual measurement.
Dimensional conformity does not substitute for surface-roughness conformity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-04.stem: The inspection sheet is revision C, while the standard on hand is revision D. What should be done before judgment?
options: Ask the responsible person which revision applies to the target product.
Ignore revisions because the equipment has a mark.
reasons: Being newer alone does not establish applicability to this product; do not adopt a revision without authorization.
Cross-check number, revision and target, and confirm with the responsible person what is specified for this product.
Reconstructing old conditions from memory does not formally verify applicability.
An equipment mark does not replace checking the document revision applicable to the product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-05.stem: “Parallelism 0.06, datum A” is specified, but the target surface is unclear. What should you do?
options: Check the indicated target and datum, including arrows, and consult about measurement.
Pass using a nearby convenient surface.
Record only the value and omit the target.
Treat parallelism as checked because length passed.
reasons: Compare the target and datum A using the feature-control frame, arrows and other indications; resolve uncertainties before finalizing the measurement method.
Choosing a convenient surface changes the formal target or datum without authorization.
A value alone does not identify which parallelism was measured; record the target surface too.
Length tolerance and parallelism are different characteristics; passing one does not verify the other.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-06.stem: You are considering initial firefighting, but the extinguisher’s suitability marking is unclear. What should you do?
options: Prioritize reporting and safe evacuation and do not attempt unsafe firefighting.
Enter the fire area to find the power supply.
reasons: Extinguishing agents suit different fires; do not treat them as identical.
Prioritize reporting and safe evacuation; do not force a response using an extinguisher of unknown suitability.
Water on oil can dangerously spread the fire and must not be used on your own judgment.
Entering the fire area to find power brings dangerous exposure to fire, smoke and electric shock.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-07.stem: A diode has a similar external shape to the component specified for amplification. Can it be substituted?
options: The same external shape means interchangeability.
Both are semiconductors, so every function is the same.
Try it and accept it if it does not heat up.
Do not replace until role, part number, terminals and ratings are verified as suitable.
reasons: Matching external shape alone does not verify compatible functions, terminals or ratings.
Even within the semiconductor category, diodes and amplification transistors have different roles.
Trial energization of an unknown component and lack of heating alone do not establish safety or functional suitability.
Do not replace until the circuit role, part number, terminals and ratings are verified against specifications.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-08.stem: A dimension is 18.00 ± 0.02 mm and the reading is 17.97 mm. Which simple limit comparison is correct?
options: Below the lower limit of 17.98 mm.
reasons: The range is 17.98–18.02 mm; 17.97 mm is not within range.
17.97 mm does not exceed the upper limit; it is below the lower limit.
Do not round conveniently to change an out-of-range reading into a pass.
The reading 17.97 mm is below the lower limit, 18.00 − 0.02 = 17.98 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-09.stem: A leak is found this morning, although yesterday’s periodic inspection passed. What should you do?
options: Record this morning’s facts and check action and whether operation is permitted.
Ignore the leak because yesterday passed.
reasons: Retain this morning’s leak as a new observation and check action and whether operation is permitted.
Yesterday’s periodic inspection does not guarantee this morning’s condition.
Recording normal after observing leakage contradicts the observation.
Internal inspection and disassembly require safety measures and authority; do not start on your own judgment.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-10.stem: An impact test shows higher absorbed energy, but temperature and specimen also differ. How should material selection proceed?
options: Treat the largest number as best for every application.
Align requirements and test conditions and confirm the valid comparison scope with the responsible person.
Average it with post-bend observations as the same quantity.
reasons: Even a larger value cannot establish superiority for every application when test conditions differ.
Erasing temperature and specimen fields loses comparison assumptions and traceability information.
Align requirements and conditions such as specimens and temperature, and verify the scope in which comparisons are valid.
Absorbed energy and post-bend crack observations are different evaluations and cannot be averaged as the same quantity.
